source.title: Optimization Landscape and Expressivity of Deep CNNs

record.file_problem: not stated; supplied text contains the full paper and appendices
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a CIFAR-unrelated MNIST training experiment and theoretical results on zero training error and critical points in wide CNNs. These bear conceptually on V1's training-error claim, but do not reproduce its CIFAR benchmark recipes.
record.gate_note: The paper cites Zhang et al. (2017) for fitting random labels; those cited results are not this study's rows. The training experiment reports MNIST results. Theorems about existence of zero-error solutions and critical points are arguments, not reported numerical outcomes, so they are not separate rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures CNN training classification error after Adam training on MNIST, extending V1's training-error question to a new dataset. It does not test the specified CIFAR settings.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: width enables linearly independent features and exact fitting, and their landscape results may help explain effective CNN training. More precisely, every critical point in the specified full-rank subset is globally optimal when the wide layer is followed by a fully connected layer; analytic activations make the subset's complement measure zero. This does not guarantee that gradient training avoids that complement or converges to zero loss. Cross-entropy is outside their analysis.
record.recipe_differences: The numerical experiment is a sigmoid CNN trained with Adam and decaying learning rate on MNIST using squared loss; the claim version concerns CIFAR convolutional networks trained with SGD or Adam, including corrupted or random labels.
record.method_sensitivity: Filter count changes the training error in the MNIST experiment: nonzero at T1=10 and 20, zero for T1≥30 in the reported sweep.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems establish finite-sample expressivity and global optimality of critical points within a full-rank parameter subset for specified wide CNN architectures. With analytic activations, its complement has Lebesgue measure zero.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under stated data, activation, width, and architecture assumptions, wide CNNs admit exact fits and have no suboptimal critical points within the specified full-rank subset. These results do not establish convergence of gradient training or frequencies of reaching bad minima.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 35th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 80, 2018
record.problems: The empirical experiment is on MNIST rather than CIFAR and uses sigmoid, Adam, and squared loss. The paper's theoretical zero-error and critical-point results require stated architecture and activation assumptions; the experiment adds Gaussian noise to meet the data-patch assumption. No uncertainty estimates or controls are reported for the training-error sweep.

untested.parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, SGD, early stopping, and regularized recipes. Random initialization is not specified for the empirical experiment. The smaller tested networks also achieve near-zero error, so this sweep does not establish substantial training error in small models.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student training, frequencies of convergence to spurious minima, and adding one or two student neurons at widths 6–20.
Depth-dependent training degradation, identity shortcuts, and training deep plain or unnormalized residual networks.
Initialization comparisons, signal or gradient propagation, training speed, and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to stability thresholds, transient loss increases, curvature dynamics, and divergence.
Batch-normalization comparisons, training speed, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source listed for these versions. Nonzero counts at 10 and 20 filters do not warrant limits_scope because V1 explicitly includes near-zero error. The empirical initialization and run-to-run variability are not reported.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, SGD, or comparisons with smaller models, early stopping, or regularized recipes. Its empirical experiment uses MNIST, sigmoid, Adam, squared loss, and decaying learning rate.
